key_insight: The study selected a 50 wt.% chamotte, 25 wt.% bakor, and 25 wt.% corundum mixture for plasma-assisted formation of a stable glass-crystalline protective layer on chamotte refractories.
engineering_relevance: The approach targets improved lining durability in metallurgy, power generation, and chemical processing through stronger adhesion and greater thermal resistance.
method: Select the coating composition using Al₂O₃–SiO₂ and Al₂O₃–SiO₂–ZrO₂ phase diagrams and melting curves.
Mill powders to 80–100 μm, mix with sodium silicate binder, apply an approximately 1 mm layer, and dry.
Treat with concentrated low-temperature plasma, then evaluate phase evolution and adhesion under thermal cycling.
evidence_signal: Evaluation included X-ray diffraction during 10 heating cycles to 1200 °C with air cooling and adhesion testing before and after cycling; the abstract reports no numerical adhesion results.
watch_item: Initial firebrick quality is critical to successful treatment, and the abstract does not establish quantitative durability gains.
paper_title: Plasma Treatment Effect on Structure and Properties of Protective Coatings for Chamotte Refractories
